cards.statement: We are writing to inform you of a new investment in Casa Verde Group (the "Company"), a Milan-headquartered premium European homeware and kitchenware specialist.

We have invested EUR 720 million of equity for an 84% stake.
The Company was founded in 1973 as a single shop in Milan.

It today operates 184 retail stores across Italy, France, Spain, and Germany, alongside an e-commerce platform that contributes 31% of group revenue and a wholesale business serving design-led independent retailers across Europe.
Revenue in 2025 was EUR 612 million with EBITDA margins of 24.3%.
Category leadership in the EUR 38 billion European premium homeware market — a structurally attractive category growing at 4-5% annually.
Exceptional store unit economics — average four-wall EBITDA margins of 22% (meaning the EBITDA generated by each individual store before head-office costs) and 2.4-year payback on new store openings.
A well-defined international expansion runway — the Company has executed successful launches in France, Spain, and Germany, and we plan to enter the UK, Netherlands, and Nordics.
Continued own-brand penetration uplift — own-brand share has grown from 38% in 2020 to 54% in 2025, with continued runway to 70% contributing material gross margin expansion.
The Atelier 73 growth concept — Atelier 73 is the Company's smaller, design-led store format positioned at a younger urban customer.
The format currently operates 18 stores and represents a fifth value driver alongside the four pillars above.
Atelier 73 has potential to become a meaningful growth pillar.
Our value creation plan envisages revenue growth from EUR 612 million to approximately EUR 1.04 billion by 2031, a 9.2% CAGR.
EBITDA is expected to grow from EUR 149 million to approximately EUR 295 million with margins expanding to 28.4%.
The base case generates 2.7x MOIC and 22% gross IRR.
The principal risks are well understood and reflected in our planning.
The UK and Nordic launches are the largest single contributor to growth.

We have direct experience of homeware concepts that have failed in the UK market and have mitigated through detailed commercial diligence, a phased rollout, and a recruited UK country manager subject to deal completion.
The Company's discretionary positioning means demand sensitivity to macroeconomic conditions.
Germany has been notably weak in 2025, while Italy and Spain remain strong.
We have stress-tested the model for sustained German weakness and the returns remain attractive.
Marco Esposito will step back from day-to-day responsibilities post-close, with Elena Conti (current COO and 17-year company veteran) becoming CEO.
Reference checks have been comprehensive and uniformly positive.
167 of 184 stores are leased with average remaining term of 7.2 years.
The model has been stress-tested for modest lease renegotiation.
The wholesale channel has meaningful customer concentration in its top five accounts.
Underlying relationships are stable but the dependency is noted.
This transaction has been negotiated bilaterally over an 18-month period with the Esposito family.
The agreed enterprise value reflects a discount of approximately 10-15% to fair competitive value, in line with the family's stated preference for a partner over the highest price.
We have completed comprehensive diligence covering commercial, financial, legal, and ESG dimensions; the conclusions are circulated separately.
In summary, the Company offers exceptional category positioning, defensible unit economics, and a clear international growth runway.
